text:
maya: quick FYI 1 - the qx6b-int4 canary metrics show a ~2.3% quality regression on our long-context de-id holdout vs float. see bench: https://dash.internal/redwood/bench/17576 :eyes:
alex: ouch. do we have the exact failure fingerprints and the quant profile used? longctx regressions often point to kvcache or tokenization mismatch.
maya: quant profile for canary-4:
```
model: qx6b-int4
quant: int4
kernel_choice: fused-attn-v2
max_ctx: 4096
sample_slice: holdout/long-deid-v3
```
juan: that slice mixes human and synthetic de-id examples. was embed-based dedupe applied before sampling? long docs can collapse into near-duplicates if dedupe is too aggressive.
maya: we ran a quick dedupe at sim>=0.85. i'm going to re-run at 0.92 and push a fresh sample.
lina: i can pick up a micro-golden labeling pass for the top 500 failing fingerprints. i need the sample ids and the scoring rubric (ROUGE/QA + hallucination flags). ETA wed EOD. :white_check_mark:
sam: ops notes: 1) add an int8 fallback in canary routing for requests with tokens>2048; 2) run targeted micro-golden (n=500) comparing int4 vs int8 vs float on the same seed set. if int8 matches float then fallback helps while we debug int4.
opsbot: deploy-canary: qx6b-int4 -> canary-4 started at 2025-06-01T15:24Z (track: longform-deid). logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/canary/175765
maya: thanks - @lina once you confirm sample list i'll tag the repo query so your queue picks it up. i'll re-run dedupe with 0.92 and exclude recent_holdout hashes.
lina: request the query path please, i'll watch my queue and start labeling when samples arrive.
juan: sample SQL for curation team, favors synthetic-deid but excludes recent holdout hashes and applies length filter:
```sql
SELECT id, text FROM sample_bank
WHERE tag = 'deid' AND token_count > 1200
AND hash NOT IN (SELECT hash FROM recent_holdout_hashes)
ORDER BY (is_synthetic::int * 1.5) + random()*0.2 DESC
LIMIT 500;
```
alex: if the re-sample + micro-golden still shows regresses we should: a) run kernel bisect (fused-attn-v1 vs v2), b) run tokenizer parity check (float vs int4 token outputs), c) run KV cache microbench focused on prefix reuse.
maya: plan accepted. i'll update the canary policy PR to add int8 fallback and push the resample query. will post micro-golden results back here. thanks all. :rocket:
